title: Evaluating Inquiry Learning in LLM-Based Agents: Hypothesizing, Reasoning, and Exploration
abstract: arXiv:2610.21604v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Scientific inquiry involves iterative cycles of exploration, hypothesis generation, and reasoning over observations to uncover relationships in complex systems. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in several components of this process, including inductive reasoning, hypothesis generation, and data analysis. However, prior work typically evaluates these abilities in isolation, leaving open how models integrate them across a full inquiry cycle. In this work, we introduce a framework for evaluating LLMs' inquiry capabilities in a unified, interactive setting. We extend the Countdown task to a mathematical environment where an agent probes the system by manipulating variables, collecting observations, and inferring relationships between them. translated_abstract: 科学探究涉及探索、假设生成以及对观察结果进行推理的迭代循环，以揭示复杂系统中的关系。大语言模型（LLM）已在这一过程的多个环节中展现出强大的能力，包括归纳推理、假设生成和数据分析。然而，先前的工作通常孤立地评估这些能力，而模型如何在完整的探究循环中整合这些能力仍是未解的问题。在这项工作中，我们引入了一个在统一、交互式环境中评估大语言模型探究能力的框架。我们将Countdown任务扩展到一个数学环境中，智能体通过操纵变量、收集观察结果并推断它们之间的关系来探测该系统。这种设置使得能够分析探究过程中的探索策略、因果发现和假设完善。在七个大语言模型和多种提示策略上，我们的……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个统一的交互式评估框架，通过将Countdown任务扩展为数学探究环境，评估大语言模型在假设生成、推理与探索这一完整科学探究循环中的综合能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a unified interactive evaluation framework that extends the Countdown task into a mathematical inquiry environment to assess LLM agents' integrated capabilities across the full scientific inquiry cycle of hypothesizing, reasoning, and exploration.
